context: A senior trains a new hire on customer phone etiquette
purpose: Teach: 申し上げる/頂く/了承/何とも/該当/どなた/告知/加わっ

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 今日は電話応対の基本を教えるよ。自分の動作には「申し上げる」を使うのが基本ね。
lines.en: Today I'll teach you phone etiquette basics. Use 'mōshiageru' for your own actions.
lines.style: Calm senior tone, instructional and measured pace.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、よろしくお願いします。電話を取った時の第一声は何と申し上げればいいですか?
lines.en: Yes, please guide me. What should I say first when I pick up the phone?
lines.style: Polite junior, slightly nervous but eager to learn.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 「お電話ありがとうございます」だね。それから相手がどなたか必ず確認すること。
lines.en: Say 'thank you for calling,' then always confirm who the caller is.
lines.style: Measured senior delivery, clear and patient instruction.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: もし担当者が不在で、該当する案件の質問を頂いた時はどうすればいいですか?
lines.en: If the person in charge is out and I get a question on the relevant matter, what do I do?
lines.style: Careful junior question, formal and respectful register.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 「ただいま席を外しております」と伝えて、折り返しお電話する旨のご了承を頂くんだ。
lines.en: Say they've stepped away, then get their consent for a callback.
lines.style: Steady senior teaching tone, demonstrating exact phrasing.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。値段や納期について聞かれたら、なかなか答えにくいですよね。
lines.en: I see. Questions about price or deadlines are really hard to answer.
lines.style: Thoughtful junior reflecting, slightly worried tone here.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: そう、即答は危険。社内に事前の告知や確認なしに約束はしないこと。何とも答えられない時は一度切るんだ。
lines.en: Right, instant answers are risky. Don't promise without prior internal notice or check. When you can't answer at all, hang up once.
lines.style: Firm senior warning, friendly but emphasizing the rule.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: わかりました。チームに加わったばかりですが、先輩の電話を横で聞いてしっかり覚えます。
lines.en: Understood. I just joined the team, but I'll listen to your calls beside you and learn properly.
lines.style: Determined junior commitment, respectful and energetic close.
